title: eve session network hops
evidence: Source-derived operation inventory, not a latency benchmark. World, cache, replay, payload size, and authored integrations change request counts.
clocks: HTTP request to first provider request
HTTP request to dispatch acceptance / returned Session identity
HTTP request to visible turn settlement

invariants.metadata: { sessionId }, accessed only when requested after resumption
invariants.startupHooks: 1 eve stable inbox + requested aliases + 1 SDK cancellation hook for the first turn

limitations: Alias-only delivery cannot distinguish an unowned address from a handoff gap. Atomic handoff is an upstream requirement.
Rows name SDK operations, not a guaranteed count of lower-level HTTP retries or queue deliveries.
Authorization, sandbox, memory, telemetry and authored hooks must be measured for a specific deployed agent.

rows.title: HTTP request + request authorization
rows.operations: 1 HTTP request; auth-dependent I/O
rows.why: Authenticate and authorize the resource before delivery. Auth provider/cache costs are application dependent.

rows.title: SDK hook lookup
rows.operations: 1 hooks.getByToken
rows.why: resumeHook(token, command) resolves the live hook and its resume context. No eve preflight; no metadata hydration.

rows.title: Try alias before creating
rows.operations: 0 for ID-only; 1 hooks.getByToken for an unowned alias
rows.why: An ID-only create goes straight to start. A missing channel alias starts a candidate immediately; an ambiguous failure does not.

rows.title: Resume payload encryption
rows.operations: 0 with stored public key; key/run reads on SDK fallback
rows.why: Current hooks carry resume context. Sealing to the public key is local; this is distinct from decrypting metadata.

rows.title: Durably accept payload
rows.operations: 1 hook_received event write
rows.why: Commit the command before publishing its wake. Backend retry/dedup capabilities control transport retries.

rows.title: Publish owner wake
rows.operations: 1 queue publish
rows.why: Targets the current owner on its pinned deployment; acceptance requires the durable write and publish.

rows.title: Return stable identity to alias caller
rows.operations: 0 hook reads; lazy metadata key access as needed
rows.why: Runs AFTER resume acceptance, concurrent with the awakened workflow. Known session addresses and forwarding-only senders do not access metadata.

rows.title: Start original session workflow
rows.operations: run_created + queue publish
rows.why: One session workflow, no child turn workflow. SDK start may overlap publication and persistence.

rows.title: Workflow activation / event history
rows.operations: run lifecycle writes + history reads, capability/replay dependent
rows.why: Queue delivery is a compute hop, not an extra producer HTTP call. Retained VM and preload paths differ from cold replay.

rows.title: Register stable inbox and initial alias
rows.operations: 1 hook_created per address; one concurrent claim batch
rows.why: One stable address, plus the requested alias. getConflict is a registration fence preventing duplicate first-turn execution, not hooks.getByToken.

rows.title: Initialize or restore session state
rows.operations: new: createSessionStep lifecycle; existing: inline snapshot hydration
rows.why: New-session initialization overlaps address claiming. Current snapshots are carried in durable step results, not fetched from a per-turn snapshot stream.

rows.title: Check idle handoff eligibility
rows.operations: isSessionIdleForHandoffStep lifecycle
rows.why: Only a fresh delivery to an idle session can trigger transfer. Same-deployment and busy sessions do not run this step.

rows.title: Register terminal anchor, first handoff only
rows.operations: 1 hook_created on original owner's first attempt
rows.why: Keeps the original run and its public stream alive after its execution ownership transfers.

rows.title: Release owned addresses and drain accepted reads
rows.operations: 1 hook_disposed per address
rows.why: If another accepted command is found, reclaim and abandon handoff. Release and claim are not atomic.

rows.title: Register activation callback and start successor
rows.operations: activation hook_created + startSessionOwnerStep lifecycle + run_created + publish
rows.why: Activation callback is registered before starting a run that can signal it. Successor receives explicit anchorRunId, snapshot, address set, deadline.

rows.title: Validate and claim transferred addresses
rows.operations: validation step lifecycle + 1 hook_created per address, batched
rows.why: No model work until all claims succeed. Preserves stable identity and uses the original stream writer.

rows.title: Acknowledge successor activation
rows.operations: signalSessionOwnerActivationStep + resume lookup/write/publish
rows.why: Old owner can now exit or park as anchor. Later owners signal the anchor only at session end.

rows.title: Start deadline workflow concurrently
rows.operations: startSessionTimeoutStep + timer run_created/publish/lifecycle + durable wait scheduling
rows.why: Default deadline infrastructure. Does not block the first model call; startup operations are joined before the session loop advances.

rows.title: SDK cancellation hook and abort stream
rows.operations: 1 abrt_* hook_created for the new turn; abort stream read
rows.why: AbortSignal transport is required for cancelling active durable steps. No eve getConflict call and no steering abort.

rows.title: Execute turnStep
rows.operations: step_started; step_created/queue delivery when not inline
rows.why: SDK may execute inline or queue a step. Registration awaiters affect inline eligibility; do not equate a step call with exactly one network request.

rows.title: Rehydrate context, deliver message, prepare model
rows.operations: local work + authored hooks/connections/sandbox I/O
rows.why: No universal count: authored integrations, dynamic model selection, memory, sandbox, and tracing can add work before the provider call.

rows.title: Resolve stream writer encryption/routing
rows.operations: run/key reads depending on writable serialization and caches
rows.why: Original owner uses getWritable(); a successor uses the anchor run's forwarded writable. Stream names are run-scoped.

rows.title: Publish pre-model events
rows.operations: stream write batches; batch count is variable
rows.why: Lifecycle events and authored handlers can be awaited before the model call. Count actual stream batches, not individual events.

rows.title: MODEL REQUEST — stop time-to-model clock
rows.operations: 1 provider request for this first call
rows.why: Provider response latency is outside time-to-model. Subsequent tool/model cycles have their own costs.

rows.title: Commit results, admit steering, settle turn
rows.operations: step_completed + optional next step + settleTurnStep + stream batches
rows.why: Steering uses the same turn after a committed boundary; queue waits for settlement. No child turn run or owner-release handshake per ordinary turn.

rows.title: Client stream observer
rows.operations: stream GET + read-key resolution as needed; tail-info only when requested
rows.why: Separate clock/branch. An already-open stream is not a new request per chunk. Reconnects target the original run.

rows.title: Optional channel activity collector
rows.operations: new root collector start; hook + activity resume/write/publish batches
rows.why: Only channels with activity renderers. Collector startup can precede session start; separate from the ordinary ID-only path.

rows.title: Explicit reset release acknowledgement
rows.operations: bounded hooks.getByToken polling after reset acceptance
rows.why: Not an ordinary send cost. Confirms the previous owner released the stable address before reset returns.

rows.title: Explicit resolveSession()
rows.operations: 1 hooks.getByToken + lazy metadata hydration
rows.why: Requested read-only identity resolution. Never used as a send preflight.

rows.title: Background task ownership resolution
rows.operations: bounded hooks.getByToken polling inside durable work
rows.why: Not the ordinary turn path. Reads runId only; no metadata hydration.
